diagnostic_evidence.quote: There exists a constant $\kappa>0$ such that, for all $(t,x)\in[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d$ and all $\xi\in\mathbb{R}^d$, \[ \xi^\top \big(\sigma(t,x)\sigma(t,x)^\top\big)\,\xi \;\ge\; \kappa\,|\xi|^2. \]

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption (ii) requires ξ^T σσ^T ξ ≥ κ|ξ|² uniformly for all (t,x) ∈ [0,T]×ℝ^d. For σ(s,x) = σ·diag(x¹,…,x^d), the matrix σσ^T = σ²·diag((x¹)²,…,(x^d)²) has minimum eigenvalue σ²·min_i(x^i)², which equals 0 whenever any component x^i = 0. Hence no positive κ exists and the claim that Assumption {assumptions} holds is false. Assumption {assumptionpde}(i) (uniform ellipticity) also fails for the same reason.

failure_location.quote: Then, it is straightforward to check that Assumptions~\ref{assumptions} and \ref{assumptionpde} hold.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either prove the penalty and discretization bounds under local (non-uniform) ellipticity with polynomial-growth transition density bounds sufficient for the local-time estimate {eq:lbound}, or replace the example with one satisfying uniform ellipticity. At minimum, a repair must withdraw the claim that Assumptions {assumptions} and {assumptionpde} hold for Black–Scholes with σ·diag(x), or restrict the state domain and re-verify all conditions there.
issues.overall_effect: All theoretical results requiring Assumption {assumptions}(ii) or {assumptionpde}(i)—including the PDE–BSDE representation (Theorem {thmpde}), the viscosity-solution penalty analysis (Proposition {apb1}, Theorem {ydiffbound}), and all downstream discretization bounds—do not apply to the paper's central motivating example or the numerical experiments of Section 5.
issues.title: Black-Scholes example violates uniform ellipticity assumption
issues.why_classification: The repair requires either relaxing a key structural hypothesis and re-verifying the viscosity/PDE arguments under weaker ellipticity (a contained but nontrivial argument) or replacing the motivating example. The method, conclusions, and rates can survive if the analysis is extended to degenerate diffusions, but the advertised scope must change.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the viscosity supersolution property of $V^\lambda$ yields \begin{equation}\label{eq:viscsuper} \mathcal{L}\phi(t_0,x_0)+f_\lambda\bigl(t_0,x_0,\phi(t_0,x_0),\sigma(t_0,x_0)\nabla\phi(t_0,x_0)\bigr)\ge 0. \end{equation}

Since $V^\lambda$ is a viscosity supersolution of the penalized PDE, we have \begin{equation} \label{T5:1} -\mathcal{L}\psi(t_0,x_0)-f_\lambda\bigl(t_0,x_0,\psi(t_0,x_0),\sigma(t_0,x_0)\nabla_x\psi(t_0,x_0)\bigr)\ge 0. \end{equation}

issues.failure_explanation: The first inequality is proved by finding a positive maximum of ℓ = p_b − V^λ − εe^{−at}Q and invoking the viscosity supersolution property (≥ 0), which yields (λ−K_y)ℓ ≤ −(ℒp_b + f) ≤ D_b⁻. For the second inequality, at a positive maximum of ℓ̂ = V^λ − p_w − εe^{−at}Q the test function touches V^λ from above, so the subsolution property (≤ 0) applies. This yields (λ−K_y)(εQ + M) ≥ ℒp_w + f, a lower bound on M rather than the needed upper bound (λ−K_y)M ≤ D_w⁺. Reversing to negative minima gives a supersolution bound on the minimum of V^λ − p_w, which controls the wrong extremum. A correct proof requires the maximum principle at the maximum of V^λ − p_w (where ∇(V^λ − p_w) = 0 gives the desired upper bound for classical solutions), adapted to viscosity solutions with nonsmooth obstacles—a nontrivial argument not supplied.

failure_location.quote: For the second inequality, one argues in the same way with \[\hat\ell(t,x):=V^\lambda(t,x)-p_w(t,x)-\varepsilon e^{-at}Q(x),\] replacing positive maxima by negative minima throughout.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide a valid proof of (λ−K_y)(p_w − V^λ)⁻ ≤ D_w⁺ for the viscosity solution V^λ, e.g., by adapting the classical maximum-principle argument to viscosity solutions on U using an Ishii-type lemma or a modified test function whose gradient matches ∇p_w at the contact point. The inequality itself appears correct.
issues.overall_effect: The bound (λ−K_y)(p_w − V^λ)⁻ ≤ D_w⁺ is used to bound the upper-obstacle penalty (Corollary stoapb), which feeds into the O(1/λ) penalty error (Theorem ydiffbound), the total penalty error (Theorem penaltyerror), the a priori estimates (Proposition xyzbound), and every downstream discretization and combined-error result.
issues.title: Second inequality of Proposition apb1 not established by stated argument
issues.why_classification: The stated inequality appears mathematically correct (the classical maximum principle gives it), but the proof requires a contained nontrivial viscosity-solution argument not supplied. All downstream results depend on this inequality, but the conclusion and rates are preserved once a valid proof is provided.

issues.failure_explanation: The BDG and triangle-inequality step yields {sup |M|^p ≤ C({sup |Y^λ|^p + |Y^λ_t|^p + (∫|f_λ|ds)^p)} but the proof writes ∫|f_λ|^p ds in place of (∫|f_λ|ds)^p. Since ∫|f_λ|^p ds ≥ N^{p−1}(∫|f_λ|ds)^p by Hölder, this larger bound cannot absorb the Z-term via the claimed 1/N factor. The subsequent combined estimate uses only (∫|f_λ|ds)^p, which does not follow from the individual bounds (ypre) and (zpre) as written. Replacing ∫|f_λ|^p ds with (∫|f_λ|ds)^p in (zpre) restores the 1/N factor from Hölder and makes the absorption valid.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace ∫|f_λ|^p ds with (∫|f_λ|ds)^p in the BDG bound (zpre), which is the quantity actually obtained from sup|M|^p ≤ C(sup|Y^λ|^p + |Y^λ_t|^p + (∫|f_λ|ds)^p). This single-line correction restores the 1/N absorption and validates the combined estimate.
issues.overall_effect: The a priori bounds ‖Y^λ‖_{S^p} + ‖Z^λ‖_{H^p} ≤ C₂ (uniform in λ) are used to bound the moments in the continuity estimate (Corollary apbcor), the discretization error (Theorem discerror), the absolute-error analysis (Theorem better), and all combined-error corollaries.
issues.title: Proposition xyzbound: wrong integrand bound in BDG step prevents absorption
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local, routine correction of one inequality in one proof step. All substantive claims and guarantees are preserved; no new lemma, construction, or argument is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: so that the balancing choice $\lambda\asymp \Delta t^{-1/2}$ yields the rate $O(\Delta t^{1/4})$ for the value process.

issues.failure_explanation: Corollary cor:added-1 bounds the root-mean-square error by C₂(λΔt^{1/2} + 1/λ). Minimizing f(λ) = λΔt^{1/2} + 1/λ gives f′(λ) = Δt^{1/2} − 1/λ² = 0, hence λ = Δt^{−1/4} and minimum value 2Δt^{1/4}. With the paper's claimed λ = Δt^{−1/2}: f = Δt^{−1/2}·Δt^{1/2} + Δt^{1/2} = 1 + Δt^{1/2} = O(1), not O(Δt^{1/4}). The correct balancing is λ ≍ Δt^{−1/4}.

failure_location.quote: In particular, if $\lambda=\Delta t^{-\frac{1}{2}}$, we obtain the minimal error rate $$\left(\max_{i\in\{0,\cdots,n-1\}}\mathbb{E}\left|Y_{t_i}-\mathcal{Y}^{\lambda,\pi}_{t_i}\right|^2\right)^{\frac{1}{2}} \le C_2 \Delta t^\frac{1}{4}$$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the stated balancing from λ ≍ Δt^{−1/2} to λ ≍ Δt^{−1/4} in the claim after Corollary cor:added-1 and in the corresponding Contributions statement. The rate O(Δt^{1/4}) itself is correct and is preserved.
issues.overall_effect: The parameter tuning recommendation for the Z-dependent mean-square error bound is wrong: choosing λ = Δt^{−1/2} yields O(1) error rather than O(Δt^{1/4}). The same erroneous balancing appears in the Contributions section (item 3). The correct O(Δt^{1/4}) rate is achievable but only with λ ≍ Δt^{−1/4}, not Δt^{−1/2}.
issues.title: Wrong optimal λ claimed for Z-dependent mean-square error rate
issues.why_classification: The correction changes the mathematical content (the optimal parameter scaling involves a different power of Δt) and the stated claim is a false mathematical assertion, not a mere typo. However, the bound itself is correct and the correct optimal rate O(Δt^{1/4}) survives with the corrected λ, so no new proof architecture is needed.
